# A grid column's renderer string resolves to its view controller's method

## Context

On dev `44534e3128`, `examples/grid/nestedRecordFields` renders its headers and no rows. Every row build throws `TypeError: column.renderer.call is not a function` at `src/grid/Row.mjs` `applyRendererOutput`, with the console reading `vdom settlement failed neo-grid-body-1`. A 13.2.0 worktree throws the same at `Row.mjs:190`, so the defect predates 13.3; it was found in an exploratory 13.3 pass (defect-note fingerprint `135c1e57c70fc633`). The operator (2026-10-17): fix it now so it can ride 13.3; the renderer string should resolve to the controller method.

## The Problem

The Country column declares `renderer: 'countryRenderer'` (`examples/grid/nestedRecordFields/Viewport.mjs:69`), and `ViewportController#countryRenderer` defines it (`ViewportController.mjs:25`). The name never reaches that method. A string renderer that only a view controller defines stays a string, and the first row that renders it throws.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.grid.column.Base#beforeSetRenderer` resolves the name with `resolveCallback(value, me)`. For a plain name, `resolveCallback` (`src/util/Function.mjs`) asks `scope.getController?.()` for a handler scope. A column is a `core.Base`, not a component, and has no `getController`, so only the column itself is searched. An `up.` name walks the column's `parent` chain.
- Unresolved, it returns the plain string. The comment there says "for view controllers to match", but no controller pass ever replaces a column's renderer.
- `Neo.grid.Container#createColumns` resolves a string renderer only against the grid Container itself (`me[renderer]`).
- A component's string handler resolves through `getController()?.getHandlerScope(name)` (`controller.Component#getHandlerScope`). The grid Container is a component, and it is the column's `parent`.
- The `rendererScope` JSDoc ranks the sources: an explicit scope, then the instance a string resolved against (`'up.name'` the ancestor, a plain name the column), then the grid Container. The #18771 fix (PR #18773) and `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/RendererScope.spec.mjs` pin that order.

## The Fix

In `beforeSetRenderer`, a plain name that neither the column nor `resolveCallback` finds is looked up through the grid's view controllers: `me.parent?.getController?.()?.getHandlerScope(name, null)`. The controller that defines the method becomes the `rendererScope`, so the method runs on it, as a component's string handler would. The column-first order stays: a name the column defines (the default `cellRenderer`, a subclass override) is never taken over by a controller method of the same name. The `rendererScope` JSDoc and the stale comment state the controller source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: A column whose plain-name renderer only a view controller above the grid defines renders through that method, with the controller as `this` (unit, `RendererScope.spec.mjs`).
- [x] AC-2: A name the column itself defines still runs on the column when a controller defines the same name (unit control).
- [x] AC-3: The existing `RendererScope.spec.mjs` arms (`up.`, function, `cellCls`, `me`/`this`, explicit scope, the `cellRenderer` controls) stay green.
- [x] AC-4: `examples/grid/nestedRecordFields` renders its rows, with the Country column showing `countryRenderer`'s country names and no console error, in a real browser.

Evidence per AC: PR #19840's AC table, at the head the operator merged (`e161f623bf`, 2026-10-17); AC-1–AC-3 ran in hosted CI's unit job, and AC-4 is the headless-Chromium render on the dev server at that head.

## Out of Scope

- Table columns' header-button scope (#18797's area).
- Clearer errors for a name nothing defines.
- Other examples.
